questions.enonce_markdown:
$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}_{(aq)} \rightarrow Fe^{3+}_{(aq)}}$

Describe how the conversion is carried out, showing clearly the reagents used and corresponding reactions. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is an **oxidation**: the iron(II) ion loses an electron, $\mathrm{Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Fe^{3+} + e^-}$.

**Reagent:** chlorine water (an oxidising agent) added to aqueous iron(II) sulphate. (Acidified potassium manganate(VII), acidified potassium dichromate(VI) or hydrogen peroxide also work.)

**Procedure and observation:** add chlorine water to the pale green iron(II) solution; the colour changes to **yellow-brown** as iron(III) forms. To confirm, add aqueous sodium hydroxide: iron(III) gives a reddish-brown precipitate (iron(II) gives a dirty green one).

**Equation:** $\mathrm{2Fe^{2+}(aq) + Cl_2(aq) \rightarrow 2Fe^{3+}(aq) + 2Cl^-(aq)}$ (charge: $+4 + 0 = +6 - 2$).

With acidified manganate(VII): $\mathrm{MnO_4^- + 8H^+ + 5Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 4H_2O + 5Fe^{3+}}$ (charge: $-1 + 8 + 10 = +17$ and $+2 + 15 = +17$); the purple colour disappears.

questions.enonce_markdown:
$\mathrm{I^-_{(aq)} \rightarrow I_{2(s)}}$

Describe how the conversion is carried out, showing clearly the reagents used and corresponding reactions. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is an **oxidation**: iodide ions lose electrons, $\mathrm{2I^- \rightarrow I_2 + 2e^-}$.

**Reagent:** chlorine water (or bromine water, acidified hydrogen peroxide or acidified potassium manganate(VII)) added to aqueous potassium iodide.

**Procedure and observation:** add chlorine water to the colourless potassium iodide solution; the solution turns **brown** and a grey-black solid (iodine) may separate. Starch solution added gives a blue-black colour, which confirms iodine.

**Equation:** $\mathrm{2I^-(aq) + Cl_2(aq) \rightarrow I_2(s) + 2Cl^-(aq)}$ (charge: $-2$ on both sides).

questions.enonce_markdown:
$\mathrm{C_2H_4 \rightarrow C_2H_6}$

Describe how the conversion is carried out, showing clearly the reagents used and corresponding reactions. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is **catalytic hydrogenation** (an addition reaction) of ethene.

**Reagents and conditions:** ethene gas and hydrogen gas passed over a finely divided **nickel catalyst** at about $150^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (platinum or palladium also work).

**Equation:** $\mathrm{C_2H_4 + H_2 \rightarrow C_2H_6}$ (C 2, H 6 on both sides). The double bond becomes a single bond and the alkene becomes an alkane.

questions.enonce_markdown:
$\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \rightarrow C_2H_6}$

Describe how the conversion is carried out, showing clearly the reagents used and corresponding reactions. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This takes **two steps**: dehydrate the ethanol to ethene, then hydrogenate the ethene.

**Step 1, dehydration:** ethanol vapour is passed over heated aluminium oxide at about $350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (or ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at $170^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$): $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \rightarrow C_2H_4 + H_2O}$ (C 2, H 6, O 1 on both sides).

**Step 2, hydrogenation:** the ethene is mixed with hydrogen and passed over a nickel catalyst at about $150^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$: $\mathrm{C_2H_4 + H_2 \rightarrow C_2H_6}$.

**Overall:** $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \rightarrow C_2H_4 \rightarrow C_2H_6}$.
